prompt: Night photograph taken with a Sony A7 IV and a 35mm f/1.8 lens, natural available light, true-to-life colour, realistic exposure and noise, documentary feel. The street-level shopfront of a small Korean fried chicken and soju restaurant on the ground floor of an older Auckland CBD building, under a covered pedestrian walkway with grey stone-tiled columns. A wide black rectangular signboard runs across the top of the shopfront; it is completely plain black with no lettering at all. Below it a central glass door with a black aluminium frame, flanked by two large glass windows. Through the glass: a dim, warm interior with corrugated metal wall panels, wooden tables and black chairs, fairy string lights, a small red-pink neon sign, a wall-mounted TV and a glowing drinks fridge. On the pavement in front: cream-white plastic outdoor chairs and small black tables. Foreground, over the shoulder of a young New Zealand woman holding up an iPhone 15 Pro; the phone screen faces the camera, large and unobstructed, and shows one perfectly uniform flat bright chroma-key green image filling the display. Her friends stand beside her chatting. A Korean man in a black t-shirt and black apron is pushing the glass door open and smiling at them. Nobody looks into the camera. No readable text anywhere, no logos, no watermark.
